(p-5) Sūrat aṣ-Ṣāffāt (The Ranks)

Makkan, and its verses number one hundred and eighty-two.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿By those who range in ranks,﴾ ﴿then those who drive away with a driving,﴾ ﴿then those who recite the Reminder.﴾ He swears by the angels who range in ranks, in the station of servanthood, in grades according to which the divine lights overflow upon them, awaiting the command of Allah; those who drive away the celestial and terrestrial bodies by the management commanded for them; or who drive people away from sins by the inspiration of good; or who drive away the devils from approaching them, who recite the signs of Allah and His sacred manifestations upon His prophets and friends; or by the categories of ordered bodies, like the closely arranged rows, and the animating spirits that govern them, and the sacred substances absorbed in the seas of holiness, glorifying Allah night and day without slackening; or by the souls of the scholars who range in worship, who drive away from disbelief and wickedness by proofs and advice, who recite the signs of Allah and His laws; or by the souls of the warriors who range in jihad, who drive away the horses, or the enemy, who recite the remembrance of Allah, which the contest with the enemy does not distract them from. The conjunction (ʿaṭf) is due to the difference of the essences, or of the attributes; and the fāʾ (then) is for the sequence of existence, as in his saying:

*Yā lahfa Ziyābata lil-Ḥārithi aṣ-Ṣābiḥi* *** *fal-ghānimi fal-āʾibi*

For the row is a perfection, and the driving is a completion by preventing evil; or the inciting toward accepting good; and the recitation is its diffusion; or the rank, as in his saying, upon him be prayers and peace: «May Allah have mercy on those who shave their heads, then those who trim» — except that it is for the excellence of the earlier over the later, and this is in the reverse. Abū ʿAmr and Ḥamzah assimilated the tāʾs into the letters that follow them, because they are close, for they come from the tip of the tongue and the roots of the incisors.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 37, verses 4–5:

﴿Indeed, your God is One.﴾ This is the answer to the oath (jawab al-qasam), and its benefit lies in magnifying the one by whom the oath is sworn and in emphasizing what is sworn to, in accordance with what is customary in their speech. As for its establishment (tahqiq), it is by His, exalted is He, saying:

﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, and Lord of the easts.﴾ For their existence and their ordering in the most perfect manner, while another arrangement was possible, is a proof of the existence of the Wise Creator and of His oneness, as has passed more than once. "Lord" (rabb) is either a substitute (badal) for "One" (wahid), or a second predicate (khabar thani), or a omitted predicate (khabar mahdhuf). "Whatever is between them" encompasses the actions of the servants, and so it indicates that these are among His creation. "The easts" (al-mashariq) are either the easts of the stars or the easts of the sun over the year, and they are three hundred and sixty points of rising, the sun rising each day at one of them, and the sunsets vary in accordance with them. For this reason He suffices with mentioning them, although the rising is more indicative of power and more eloquent as a blessing. And what has been said, that they are one hundred and eighty, is only valid if the times of transition did not vary.

﴿Indeed, We have adorned the nearest heaven﴾, the one nearer to you. ﴿with an adornment of the stars﴾: with an adornment that is the stars, and the idafa (genitive construction, here explanatory, "adornment, namely the stars") is for specification. This is supported by the reading of Hamza, Ya'qub and Hafs, who read *zinatin* with tanwin and *al-kawakib* in the genitive, making it a substitution (badal) for it. Or (the adornment is) an adornment belonging to them, such as their lights and their positions. Or (the meaning is) that We adorned the stars within it, with the verbal noun annexed to its object. For it, as it came as an ism (noun) like *al-liqa* (the state of meeting), it came also as a masdar (verbal noun) like *al-nisba* (the state of being related). This is confirmed by the reading of Abu Bakr with tanwin and nasb (accusative), in its original form. Or (the meaning is) that their adornment is the stars, with the idafa taken to the agent, and with the fixed stars being set in the eighth sphere. As for the planets other than the moon, which lie in the six intermediate spheres between them and the nearest heaven, even if this is established, it does not undermine this, for the people of the earth see them all as luminous, sparkling jewels upon their blue surface, in various shapes.

﴿And as a protection﴾ is in the accusative by an implied verb, or it is coordinated with *zinatin* according to the sense, as if he had said: "We created the stars as an adornment for the nearest heaven and as a protection." ﴿from every rebellious devil﴾, one who has come out of obedience, by being pelted with shooting stars.

The commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on Surah 37, verses 8–10:

﴿They cannot listen to the exalted assembly﴾. This is a new (*mubtada'*, independent) sentence (a sentence that begins a new clause, not dependent on what precedes it) explaining their condition after the heavens were guarded against them. It is not permissible to make it a qualifier (*sifah*, descriptive clause) of every devil, for that would imply that the guarding was from devils who do not hear. There is no reason for the guarding to be read as if the *lam* had been omitted, as in *ji'tuka an tukrimani* ("I came to you that you honour me"), where *an* was then dropped and its effect nullified, as in his saying:

*Alā ayyuhādhā al-zājiri aḥḍir al-waghā*
("Oh you who forbid me, be present at the battle")

The gathering of these things is objectionable. The pronoun refers to *kull* (every) in terms of its meaning. The verb "listen" is followed by *ilā* because it implies the sense of "attending closely," for emphasis in negating it and to magnify what prevents them from it. This is supported by the reading of Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Hafs with the doubled consonant, from *tasammu'* (eavesdropping), which means seeking to hear. *Al-Mala' al-A'la* (the exalted assembly) means the angels and their nobles.

﴿And they are pelted﴾, that is, they are struck. ﴿From every side﴾, from the sides of the heaven, when they intend to ascend to it.

﴿Repulsion﴾ is a reason (*'illah*, purpose clause): meaning, for the sake of repulsion, which is driving away. Or it is a verbal noun (*maṣdar*), since it and *qadhf* (pelting) are close in meaning. Or it is a circumstantial state (*ḥal*) meaning "repelled." Or it is *dahr* (plural *duḥūr*) with the preposition removed, which is what is driven away with. The reading with a *fatḥah* supports this. It may also be a verbal noun like *qabūl* (acceptance), or a qualifier of it, meaning "pelting, repelling."

﴿And for them is a punishment﴾, that is, another punishment. ﴿Perpetual﴾ means lasting or severe, and this is the punishment of the Hereafter.

﴿Except one who snatches a snatch﴾. This is an exception from the *waw* of *yassamma'ūna* (they listen), and *man* is a substitute (*badal*, replacement) for it. *Al-khaṭf* means snatching away, and what is meant is stealing the speech of the angels stealthily. For this reason the snatch is made definite. It is also read *khaṭṭafa* with doubling, with the *kha'* open or with a *kasrah*, and its origin is *ikhtaṭafa*. ﴿Then a flaming fire pursued him﴾. *Atba'a* means the same as *tabi'a* (to follow). *Al-shihāb* is what is seen as if a star had shot down. What is said, that it is a vapour rising to the upper air and then catching fire, is a conjecture. If it is correct, it does not contradict this, since there is nothing in it indicating that it falls from the sphere, nor in His saying: ﴿And We have adorned the lowest heaven with lamps, and made them missiles against the devils﴾. For every luminous body that appears in the high atmosphere is a lamp for the people of the earth and an adornment of the heaven, in that it is seen as if it were on its surface. It is not far-fetched that the event, as mentioned, may at some times become a stoning of devils who ascend near the sphere to eavesdrop. As for what is related, that this event occurred at the birth of the Prophet (ﷺ), if it is correct, then perhaps what is meant is the frequency of its occurrence, or its becoming a repulsion. It is disputed whether the one who is stoned is harmed by it so that he turns back, or whether he is burned by it. But it may strike the ascender once and may not strike him at other times, like the wave for the rider of a ship. For this reason they do not refrain from it entirely. It is not said that the devil is made of fire and so is not burned, because he is not of pure fire, just as man is not of pure earth, and because a strong fire, when it overpowers a weak one, consumes it. ﴿Piercing﴾ means shining, as if it pierces the air with its light.

**﴿So ask them﴾**, meaning seek information from them. The pronoun refers to the polytheists of Makkah, or to the children of Adam.

**﴿Are they more difficult to create, or those We have created?﴾** That is, what was mentioned: the angels, the heavens, the earth, what lies between them, the easts, the stars, and the piercing shooting stars. The word **﴿مَن﴾** (man) is used here to give precedence (*taghlib*, giving precedence to one category over another) to rational beings (*al-'uqala'*). This is shown by its absolute use and by its coming after that, and by the reading of the one who reads **«أمْ مَن عَدَدْنا»** (*am man 'adadna*), a reading attributed to some reciters.

And His saying: **﴿Indeed, We created them from clay that sticks.﴾** This is what distinguishes them from the others, not what distinguishes them from those before them, such as 'Ad and Thamud. The purpose is to establish the return (*al-ma'ad*, the resurrection) and to refute its impossibility (*istihalah*). The matter concerning it is the same whether applied to them or to those before them. Its explanation is that the impossibility of this is either due to the matter not being receptive, and their original material is the clay that sticks, which results from joining the watery component to the earthy component, and both of these remain and are still capable of being joined. They know that the first human was produced from it, either because they acknowledge the origination of the world, or because of the story of Adam. And they have witnessed the generation of many animals from it without the mediation of sexual intercourse. So it is necessary for them to allow that they can be restored in the same way. Or the impossibility is due to the inability of the agent, but whoever is able to create these things is able to do what is not considered great in comparison with them, especially since their first creation is among that, and His power is essential and does not change.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 37, verses 12–14:

﴿Nay, you marvel﴾ at the power of God, exalted is He, and at their denial of the Resurrection. ﴿And they mock﴾ at your wonder and at your affirmation of the Resurrection. Ḥamzah and al-Kisa'i read it with a ḍammah on the tā' (i.e., ﴿wa-yusakhkhar﴾ / "and they are mocked"), meaning: the perfection of My power and the abundance of My creatures has reached the point that you marvelled at them, while these people, out of their ignorance, mock them. Or: you marvelled that the Resurrection should be denied by One whose deeds are such, while they mock those who consider it possible. The marvelling attributed to God, exalted is He, is either by way of supposition and imagination, or in the sense of the magnification that necessarily accompanies it, for it is a startled awe that seizes a person when he magnifies something. It has also been said that it is governed by an implied "say" (qawl), i.e., He said: "O Muhammad, nay, you marvel."

﴿And when they are reminded, they do not remember﴾: when they are admonished with something, they do not take admonition from it; or, when there is mentioned to them what indicates the soundness of the gathering (ḥashr), they do not benefit from it, because of their dullness and the paucity of their reflection.

﴿And when they see a sign﴾: a miracle that indicates the truthfulness of the one who brings it. ﴿They mock it excessively﴾: they exaggerate in ridicule and say: "It is sorcery." Or: some of them urge one another to mock it.

﴿And when they are reminded, they do not remember﴾: when they are admonished with something, they do not take admonition from it; or, when there is mentioned to them what indicates the soundness of the gathering (ḥashr), they do not benefit from it, because of their dullness and the paucity of their reflection.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 37, verses 12–14:

﴿Nay, you marvel﴾ at the power of God, exalted is He, and at their denial of the Resurrection. ﴿And they mock﴾ at your wonder and at your affirmation of the Resurrection. Ḥamzah and al-Kisa'i read it with a ḍammah on the tā' (i.e., ﴿wa-yusakhkhar﴾ / "and they are mocked"), meaning: the perfection of My power and the abundance of My creatures has reached the point that you marvelled at them, while these people, out of their ignorance, mock them. Or: you marvelled that the Resurrection should be denied by One whose deeds are such, while they mock those who consider it possible. The marvelling attributed to God, exalted is He, is either by way of supposition and imagination, or in the sense of the magnification that necessarily accompanies it, for it is a startled awe that seizes a person when he magnifies something. It has also been said that it is governed by an implied "say" (qawl), i.e., He said: "O Muhammad, nay, you marvel."

﴿And when they are reminded, they do not remember﴾: when they are admonished with something, they do not take admonition from it; or, when there is mentioned to them what indicates the soundness of the gathering (ḥashr), they do not benefit from it, because of their dullness and the paucity of their reflection.

﴿And when they see a sign﴾: a miracle that indicates the truthfulness of the one who brings it. ﴿They mock it excessively﴾: they exaggerate in ridicule and say: "It is sorcery." Or: some of them urge one another to mock it.

﴿And they say, "This is only"﴾ meaning what they see. ﴿clear magic﴾, its magic being evident.

﴿"When we have died and become dust and bones, shall we indeed be resurrected?"﴾ Its original form was أنُبْعَثُ (anub'athu, "shall we be raised") إذا مِتْنا (idha mitna, "when we have died"). They changed the verbal construction to a nominal one, placed the adverbial phrase first, and repeated the interrogative hamza (أ) for emphasis in denial, and to indicate that resurrection is itself deemed unlikely, and in this state it is even more strongly deemed unlikely. Thus it is more eloquent than the reading of Ibn 'Amir (qira'at, recited readings), which omits the first hamza, and the reading of Nafi', al-Kisa'i and Ya'qub, which omits the second.

﴿"And our forefathers of old?"﴾ It is conjoined either to the position (mahall) of inna (إنَّ, "indeed") and its subject, or to the pronoun in "mab'uthun" (مَبْعُوثُونَ, "resurrected"), since it is separated from it by the interrogative hamza, to add to the sense of improbability because of the remoteness of their time. Nafi', through the transmission of Qalun, and Ibn 'Amir pronounced the waw (و) as a sukun, to convey the sense of alternation (tardid).

﴿Say, "Yes, and you will be abased."﴾ Daakhirun (داخِرُونَ) means saghirun (صاغِرُونَ), "humbled." He was content with mentioning it only in the answer because what indicates its possibility had already preceded, and the miracle stands as proof of the truth of the one who reports its occurrence. It was also read as "qala" (قالَ, "he said"), i.e., God or the Messenger. Al-Kisa'i alone read na'am (نِعَمْ) with a kasra, and this is a dialectal variant of it.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 37, verse 19–21:

﴿Then it will be but one shout﴾ — the response to an implied condition, meaning: if that is the case, then the resurrection is but (a zajrah, "a single shout") — one single cry, which is the second blast (al-nafkhah al-thaniyah), like the shout of a shepherd at his sheep when he calls out to them and commands them to return. The command for the restoration is like the command "Be!" (kun) in the originating of creation, and for this reason it is ordered upon it. ﴿And behold, they will be looking﴾ — meaning, they will suddenly be standing up from their resting places, alive, seeing, or waiting to see what will be done to them.

﴿And they will say: "Woe to us! This is the Day of Recompense."﴾ — the day on which we are repaid for our deeds. With this, their speech is complete. Then His saying:

﴿"This is the Day of Judgement which you used to deny."﴾ — this is the answer of the angels. It was also said that it is likewise part of the speech of some of them to others. Al-fasl means the judgement (al-qada'), or the distinction between the good-doer and the wrongdoer.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 37, verses 22–23:

﴿Gather those who did wrong﴾. This is a command of God to the angels, or a command of some of them to others, to gather the wrongdoers from their station to the place of standing (al-mawqif).

It was also said: from there to Hellfire (al-Jahim). ﴿And their spouses﴾, meaning their likes: the worshipper of an idol with the idol-worshippers, and the worshipper of a star with its worshippers, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And you shall be three kinds (azwajan thalathah)﴾. Or it means their wives who followed their religion, or their companions among the devils. ﴿And what they used to worship﴾ ﴿besides God﴾: the idols and other things, as an increase in their humiliation and shame. This is a general statement specified by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us﴾, and so on. In it is evidence that those who did wrong are the polytheists. ﴿So guide them to the path of Hellfire﴾: make known to them the way so that they may follow it.
